[[Denise Crosby]] (primary) }} {{aquote|Everything in me that was Human died [[2349|that day]] with my mother. All that's left is Romulan. Never doubt that.|Sela|2368|Redemption II}} [[Commander]] '''Sela''' was a [[military]] [[officer]] in the [[Romulan military]], and an extremely important figure in [[Romulan Star Empire|the Empire]]'s covert attempts to destabilize both the [[Federation]] and the [[Klingon Empire]]. She was the product of a union between [[Starfleet]] officer [[Tasha Yar]]'s [[Natasha Yar#Alternate timelines|counterpart]] from an [[alternate timeline]] and a [[Sela's father 001|Romulan general]]. == Events leading to birth == In the year [[2344]], while in the middle of a [[Battle of Narendra III|battle]] with four [[Romulan warbird (2340s)|Romulan Warbirds]], the {{USS|Enterprise|NCC-1701-C|-C}} traveled through a [[temporal rift]] to the year [[2366]]. This had the effect of creating an [[alternate timeline]], wherein the Federation was at [[Federation-Klingon War (alternate timeline)|war]] with the Klingon Empire, and Tasha Yar had not died at [[Vagra II]]. Emerging from the rift, the ''Enterprise''-C encountered its successor, the {{USS|Enterprise|NCC-1701-D|-D}}. Through [[Guinan]], the ''Enterprise''-D crew learned that, in order for the timeline to be restored, the ''Enterprise''-C had to return through the rift, even though doing so would almost certainly mean their deaths. Learning from Guinan that, in the other timeline, she had died a meaningless death, Tasha requested and was granted a transfer to the ''Enterprise''-C, which returned through the rift and resumed the battle with the Romulans. ({{TNG|Yesterday's Enterprise}}) == Early life == [[File:Natasha Yar, 2366 - alternate timeline.jpg|thumb|left|Tasha Yar, Sela's mother]] While the ''Enterprise''-C was destroyed, several [[crew]]members survived and were taken prisoner by the [[Romulan]]s, Tasha among them. After being [[interrogate]]d, all of the survivors were to be [[execute]]d, but a [[Sela's father 001|Romulan general]] became enamored with Tasha, and offered to spare the lives of the prisoners if she became his consort, a condition to which Tasha agreed. [[2345|One year later]], she gave birth to a daughter, Sela. When Sela was [[2349|four years]] old, Tasha took her and attempted to escape, but sensing that her mother was attempting to take her away from her home and her father, Sela cried out, and Tasha was discovered and subsequently executed. ({{TNG|Redemption II}}) == Military career == Over the next [[2367|eighteen years]], Sela rose through the ranks of the Romulan military, achieving the rank of [[Commander]]. In that capacity, she was a major player in plots to disrupt the alliance between the Federation and the Klingon Empire, one of which involved [[kidnapping]] [[Starfleet]] [[officer]] [[Geordi La Forge]], and [[brainwashing]] him to kill [[Klingon]] [[governor]] [[Vagh]]. ({{TNG|The Mind's Eye}}) She was also involved in lending support to the [[House of Duras]] in their attempt to gain control of the Klingon Empire, ferrying them materials and supplies in [[cloak]]ed Romulan vessels. Sela was foiled, however, when [[Captain]] [[Jean-Luc Picard]] led [[Starfleet]] to the [[Klingon-Romulan border]] and instituted a [[tachyon detection grid]], making it impossible for any cloaked ship to cross the border undetected. Data, in command of the {{USS|Sutherland|NCC-72015}}, managed to use the [[tachyon]] signature that formed around Sela's ships, and ordering three [[photon torpedo]]es, lit up the [[tachyon field]] around the three cloaked Romulan [[Warbird]]s, causing them to reveal themselves, forcing Sela to withdraw back to Romulan space, causing the House of Duras to lose the [[Klingon Civil War|civil war]]. ({{TNG|Redemption|Redemption II}}) Sela was encountered again in [[2368]], when she masterminded a plot to [[invade]] {{dis|Vulcan|planet}}, exploiting [[Ambassador]] [[Spock]]'s underground [[Vulcan reunification|reunification]] movement on [[Romulus]]. Using three stolen [[Apollo class|Vulcan ships]] carrying a Romulan invasion force, she attempted to use Spock to convince the Federation that a peace [[envoy]] was en route to Vulcan. Spock refused, however, forcing Sela to use a preprogrammed hologram of Spock as an alternative. She then made the mistake of leaving Spock alone with Picard and Data, the latter having become proficient with Romulan computer systems. When Sela returned to her captives, she was captured instead and was forced to watch as Data foiled her plot by warning the Federation, forcing the cloaked warbird escorting the stolen Vulcan ships to destroy them rather than let them be captured, before the [[android]] used a [[Vulcan nerve pinch]] on Sela, incapacitating her. ({{TNG|Unification I|Unification II}}) == Appendices == === Appearances ===
* {{TNG}} **{{e|The Mind's Eye}} **{{e|Redemption}} **{{e|Redemption II}} **{{e|Unification II}}
=== Background information === Sela was devised and portrayed by [[Denise Crosby]]. In devising the role, Crosby stated, "''the part of Sela sort of came about from me sitting around in my house one day thinking about how much fun it was for me to go back and do {{e|Yesterday's Enterprise}}, and it was so much fun that I thought what else can I do? I thought it was pretty well established that Lt. Yar and Lt. [[Richard Castillo|Castillo]] on "Yesterday's Enterprise" had something going so perhaps they had a child or Yar was pregnant when she went back into the past to fight her final battle. And I sort of thought it out and it seemed to really make sense, and there were no flaws.''" "''So my original intention was that Lt. Yar would have a daughter that was raised by Romulans and would grow up to try to actually be a Romulan. So I brought this up and the producers really liked the idea and they sort of toyed with it for a while. A few months went by and I got a call and they said we like your idea but we just can't make sense of that Lt. Yar got pregnant by Castillo. We'll have it so that Yar was captured, they didn't all die in the battle, the ship was captured and she was taken by a Romulan general.''" (''[[Trek: The Next Generation Crew Book]]''{{page cite}}) In her first appearance in the episode "The Mind's Eye", Crosby only lent her voice to this character although uncredited. Actress [[Debra Dilley]] appeared as the [[photo double]] standing in the shadows. She was identified as "Unseen Woman" in the character section of the episode's [[script]], and noted as being one of "several shadowy figures [who] might be A WOMAN, but it's hard to be sure," it is further noted when she speaks, she has "a questioning, authoritative tone in her voice." The only other revelation about the character is her being addressed as "Commander". {{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/198.txt}} In her second appearance, she was identified as "Mysterious Woman" in the character section of the episode's script, and presented much the same way in the script notes, her as "ANOTHER FIGURE sitting in he darkness […] who might be a woman, but we're not sure yet," which further notes, "''The Woman in shadow doesn't have to raise her voice in order to command everyone's attention instantly. There is something deadly in her calm voice and assured manner.''" In the moments leading up to her reveal, the script notes that "the Mysterious Woman heard from earlier is sitting in a chair with her back to us," and "the Woman turns around in her chair so that her features become apparent for the first time. We're shocked as we see that she's Human… with blonde hair… and that she bears a striking resemblance to the late Tasha Yar." {{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/200.txt}} In {{e|Redemption II}}, [[Cameron]] served as [[hand double]] for Crosby's character. According to the script, her name was pronounced SEE-lah, and it was said "''Sela's attitude is crisp, dispassionate… very Romulan. B'Etor is very deferential to Sela… she clearly fears her.''" Her personality is further explored after she enters the conference room aboard the ''Enterprise'', where the script notes described that "''Sela immediately strides into the room, looking around, pacing like a jungle cat, covering the room as though marking territory. She is lithe, genial, confident -- and definitely going for the upper hand.''" The script notes continue, through the continuation of their interaction, that she slowly loses her upper hand to the challenges made by Picard. {{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/201.txt}} Her character is further addressed as "Commander", and in fact, she even appears to given orders to the seemingly senior officer, General Movar, on nearly all their interactions. Though Sela states how Tasha, her mother, died when she was four while trying to escape, Picard is completely unconvinced that her story is true, and insists it won't affect his judgment in any way. Sela's story is supported by Guinan, who retains memories from the alternate timeline shown in {{e|Yesterday's Enterprise}}. Sela has the distinction of being the first blonde Romulan seen in ''[[Star Trek]]'', and the only blonde Romulan seen until the {{s|PIC}} episode {{e|Absolute Candor}}. === Apocrypha === Sela returned to plague [[Captain]] [[Jean-Luc Picard]] and company several more times in the ''Star Trek'' [[novels]], notably in [[Peter David]]'s books ''[[Triangle: Imzadi II]]'', in which she attempted to trick [[Thomas Riker]] into releasing a nanovirus that would destroy the entire Klingon population on their homeworld; the plan was thwarted by the intervention of [[William T. Riker]], [[Worf]] and [[Odo]]. Another notable return was in book five of the ''[[Double Helix]]'' series ''[[Double or Nothing]]''. In the book ''[[The Romulan Stratagem]]'', Sela forms an alliance with [[Data]] to uncover the truth about a series of disastrous events that cast suspicion on both the Romulans and the Federation. She later appears in [[Michael Jan Friedman]]'s TNG relaunch novel ''[[Death in Winter]]'', as an agent of the Romulan government formed by the newly ascended [[Praetor]] [[Tal'aura]], whose other allies include [[Tomalak]]. During the ''[[Star Trek: Typhon Pact|Typhon Pact]]'' series, Sela has become the head of the Tal Shiar, mounting various operations to try and steal the technology for the [[Quantum slipstream drive]] from the Federation. After her actions result in the destruction of [[Deep Space 9]] and the Federation and the Pact nearly being pushed to war in the novel ''[[Raise the Dawn]]'', Sela is arrested by the current Praetor – who notes that Sela's desire to ensure Romulan supremacy have actually put them in more danger than if she had done nothing – and Sela commits suicide rather than allow herself to be handed over to the Federation for trial. The novelization of ''{{dis|Unification|novel}}'' gives the name of the Romulan general who fathers Sela as "Meldet", while the novel ''[[Vulcan's Heart]]'' calls him "Volskiar". The ''[[Star Trek: Defiant Annual]]'' calls him "Revo". Sela also appeared, with the rank of [[Admiral]], in the [[computer]] [[game]] ''[[Star Trek: Armada]]''. Further, in the {{comic}} miniseries ''[[Star Trek: The Next Generation - The Killing Shadows]]'' by [[Scott Ciencin]] and [[Andrew Currie]], Sela resurfaces as an exile from [[Romulus]], serving alongside Picard on the planet Nydaris in common cause against a race of ninja-like assassins called the Bodai Shin. [[File:TacticalCommanderSela.webp|thumb|Sela's description as a crewmember on the USS ''Defiant''.]] In the ''[[Star Trek: Defiant|Defiant]]'' series, Sela forms an [[alliance]] with [[Commander]] [[Worf]] and his rogue crew – who include [[Spock]], [[B'Elanna Torres|B’Elanna Torres]], [[Ro Laren]] and [[Lore]] – to thwart the ambitions of the renegade [[Klingon emperor]] [[Kahless (clone)|Kahless]] and his [[cult]] of followers, the {{mb|Red Path|Red Path}}, who have recruited Romulans to their ranks and stolen valuable [[military]] resources from the Star Empire. As a result, she journeys to [[Qo'noS|Qo’noS]] with the rest of the ''[[USS Defiant (2375)|Defiant]]'' crew and, joining forces with [[Captain]] [[Benjamin Sisko]] and the {{mb|USS Theseus (NX-1987)|USS ''Theseus''}}, helps to stop the Day of Blood, during which she helped to save the life of [[Chancellor of the Klingon High Council|Chancellor]] [[Martok]]. At this point, Sela’s position within the [[Tal Shiar]] had been severely compromised. Though she admits to having had her fair share of accomplishments while fighting [[Dominion]]-[[Breen-Dominion Alliance|allied]] [[Breen]] in the [[Dominion War|war]], her previous failures in both the [[Klingon Civil War]] and attempted takeover of [[Vulcan]] have damaged her [[career]]. As such, she sought to use the destruction of the Red Path and its roots within her own people to boost her standing, coercing Martok into sharing several defence secrets with her. Despite this, her position remains precarious, and Sela later tries to [[Time travel|go back]] in [[time]], but found herself encouraging a past version of [[Natasha Yar|her mother]], who she was unable to [[Murder|execute]], despite initially planning to do so. This event caused Sela to reconsider her perspective, and she subsequently comes to the rescue of her former allies onboard the ''Defiant'' crew at {{mb|Starbase 99}}, which has been overrun by [[Parasitic being|parasitic beings]] from another [[dimension]]. Arriving just in time, Sela proceeds to assist both Worf and Spock in closing the gateway between their two dimensions, which results in the apparent [[death]] of {{mb|Nymira Vondect|Nymira Vondect}}. Shortly after this victory, however, the ''Defiant'' and its personnel - Sela included - are captured by her father {{mb|Revo|General Revo}}, who convinces his daughter to turn on her comrades. The two then take Spock prisoner and [[Extortion|blackmail]] his three teammates - Worf, B'Elanna and Ro - into kidnapping [[Chairman]] [[Koval]] and [[Praetor]] [[Neral]], enabling them to declare [[martial law]] and put a ''[[coup d'état]]'' into motion, framing their allies as members of a fictional [[Terrorism|terrorist]] group. Sela, however, turns against her father and aids her old enemy Spock in his escape, learning the truth of what Revo was hiding: that an effort to protect [[Romulus]] during the Dominion War triggered events that caused their [[Romulus (star)|star]] to become unstable, leading to the impending [[supernova]] that was fated to destroy the planets of their [[Romulus system|system]]. After learning this, Sela - daughter of Revo and Tasha Yar, operative of the Tal Shair and one-time nemesis of Spock - overcomes her father and issues a public broadcast where she declares her allegiance to the {{Mb|Hand of Ganmadan|fictional organisation}} that she had claimed the ''Defiant'' crewmembers belonged to, thereby becoming a wanted criminal, while Spock sets out his plans to help evacuate the Romulan star system. In ''[[Star Trek Online]]'', Sela became Proconsul in 2384, but was exiled from Romulus after losing a power struggle with the [[Tal Shiar]]. As a result, she survived the [[Unnamed Alpha and Beta Quadrant stars#Supernova of 2387|Hobus supernova of 2387]] that destroyed Romulus and killed many of her political opponents. In 2403, she becomes Praetor, and five years later reforms the Empire into a monarchy, with herself as its Empress. In the game itself, the player encounters Sela in the mission "Cutting the Cord," where the player must fight her personal ''[[Scimitar]]''-class warbird, the IRW ''Leahval''. Before the player can destroy it, an [[Iconian]] ship arrives from an [[Iconian gateway]] and tows her ship to an unknown location. Her role was greatly expanded in the May 2013 ''Legacy of Romulus'' expansion pack, where she serves as a secondary villain in the Romulan Republic storyline (the primary antagonist being [[Colonel]] Hakeev of the Tal Shiar). In the October 2014 ''Delta Rising'' expansion, Sela is found in an [[Shroomies|Elachi]] installation hidden in the [[Delta Quadrant]], and arrested by the Romulan Republic. However, she escapes, and solicits the aid of the player character to find the Iconians; they travel first to Hakeev's abandoned base in the Nopada system, and then to a [[Dyson sphere]] in the [[Andromeda Galaxy]], where they encounter the renegade Praetor [[Taris]] and discover a massive Iconian invasion fleet. The sphere then shifts to orbit around [[Iconia]] itself, and Sela remains behind while the players escape. A series of subspace messages to the player reveal that she is attempting to gather [[Dominion]] support against the Iconians. During the final battle of the Iconian War at [[Earth]], Sela returns with Dominion reinforcements in order to buy time for a time travel mission to ancient Iconia using a [[Krenim weapon ship]]. In retaliation for the destruction of Romulus, Sela kills several Iconians as they flee through gateways, causing the Iconians to swear vengeance on the Romulans. This leads to a [[predestination paradox]]: Sela, in her desire to avenge the destruction of Romulus, was in fact the reason it occurred. Sela returns in the mission "Survivor", where the player character hunts her down at the suggestion of [[Agent]] {{dis|Daniels|Crewman}} to help search for the alternate timeline version of Admiral T'Nae. Sela agrees, understanding she's effectively under arrest. During their search, they find datapads revealing that her mother was never killed, instead left with the rest of the crew of the ''Enterprise''-C on a prison colony, shaking Sela greatly. Over the course of the mission, Sela learns that Yar always loved Sela and wished she could see her, sadly being unable to as she died of natural causes before the player could arrive. After being put under arrest, Sela asks an unknown Starfleet officer (implied to be [[Data]], as he shows his holoimage of Tasha to her, though his face is not seen) to tell her more about Tasha. === External links === * {{mbeta}} * {{STOwiki}} [[de:Sela]] [[es:Sela]] [[it:Sela]] [[pt:Sela (Star Trek)]] [[Category:Romulans]] [[Category:Humans]] [[Category:Hybrids]] [[Category:Romulan military personnel]]

{{sidebar individual |image = Li Nalas in uniform.jpg |caption = Li Nalas (2370) |species = [[Bajoran]] |occupation = [[Navarch]] and [[Bajoran]] [[liaison officer]] on board [[Deep Space 9]] |status = [[Deceased]], killed saving [[Commander]] [[Benjamin Sisko|Sisko]] |died = [[2370]] |datestatus = 2370 |actor = [[Richard Beymer]] }} {{aquote|Li Nalas was ''the'' hero of the Bajoran resistance. He performed extraordinary acts of courage for his people and died for their freedom.|Benjamin Sisko|2370|The Siege}} '''Li Nalas''' was the leader of one of [[Bajor]]'s many [[Bajoran Resistance|resistance cells]] during the [[Cardassian]] [[Occupation of Bajor]]. A revered war hero, he was considered by many to be the greatest [[Bajoran]] resistance fighter ever. == History == === Early life and the resistance === Prior to his time in the Resistance, Li had spent time working in [[Terok Nor]]'s [[ore processing center]]. Later, Li was part of a minor resistance cell. When they were in the [[mountain]]s surrounding the [[Sahving Valley]], the cell was [[ambush]]ed by the [[Cardassian]]s. Li and two others survived. After two [[day]]s hiding in the hills, they were forced by a lack of [[food]] and [[water]] into the [[valley]]. They made their way to a ridge overlooking a small [[lake]]. As Li was the only one with a [[phaser]], he left his companions and scouted ahead for the enemy. About halfway down the embankment, he stumbled and landed on his back just as a tall Cardassian emerged from the water. He was a [[gul]] in the [[Cardassian military]], and he might have just been bathing in the lake. There was a pause, as the two were frozen in surprise – Li lying on his back, stunned, on the shore and the Cardassian, embarrassed in his [[underwear]], shivering from the cold. Acting first, Zarale reached for his [[phaser rifle]], which was lying on his clothes, on a nearby [[rock]]; however, before he could fire his rifle, Li fired his phaser and [[death|killed]] the gul. The gul's body collapsed onto Li. Moments later, this was how Li's companions found him. Upon finding him and the dead gul, one of his companions identified the gul as [[Zarale]], who was responsible for the massacre of half a dozen [[Bajoran]] [[village]]s. Before Li could explain how he came about killing the gul, his companions, convinced there was a savage struggle between the Zarale and Li, began spreading their story of how Li killed the gul. Efforts by Li of denying his companions' story failed, as he became a legend in the resistance and victories were attributed to his leadership. His exploits spread and grew to mythic proportions. [[File:Li Nalas.jpg|thumb|Li Nalas' rescue in 2370]] Li Nalas' career as a resistance fighter ended with his capture in [[2360]]. Although his body was never found, he was presumed [[killed in action]] until [[2370]], when he was rescued from the [[Hutet]] [[labor camp]] on [[Cardassia IV]] by [[Major]] [[Kira Nerys]] of the [[Bajoran Militia]] and [[Miles O'Brien]] who posed as prostitute and her pimp, respectively, to gain access to the camp. In the camp, he was an inspiration to the other Bajoran captives. ({{DS9|The Homecoming}}) === Bajoran hero === After he and his fellow prisoners were rescued, Li was taken to [[Deep Space 9]] where he was immediately recognized. He was very uncomfortable with his status as a hero and attempted to secretly leave the station for the [[Gamma Quadrant]]. Discovered by the crew of the departing ship, he was returned to [[Commander]] [[Benjamin Sisko]]. After Sisko questioned Li and pressed him for an explanation, he admitted that the stories of his heroism were largely based on myth. Li told the truth behind the myth that surrounded his reputation. As Li would relate to Sisko, he would never forget the embarrassed look on the Cardassian officer's face as he died in his underwear. Li confided in Sisko that he had always felt uncomfortable with being an accidental hero. Sisko confronted Li with the unfortunate truth that Bajor needed a symbol; someone that the people could believe in because the planet was on the verge of [[civil war]]. [[File:Odo presents evidence.jpg|thumb|left|Serving as liaison officer to Deep Space 9]] Shortly after his return to Bajor, Li was given both the title of [[Navarch]] and Kira's position as Bajoran [[liaison officer]] on board [[Deep Space 9]], much to his embarrassment. Li assured Sisko that he would do his best to fulfill his duties but that he could never replace Kira. This was done by [[Minister]] [[Jaro Essa]], who wanted to get Kira out of a position of power and to get Li off Bajor so that he would not influence Jaro's plot to take over the government. ({{DS9|The Homecoming|The Circle}}) His rescue proved to be just in the nick of time, as he was able to play a pivotal role in preventing a disastrous ''[[coup d'état]]'' orchestrated by the [[Alliance for Global Unity]]. He helped rescue Kira from the insurgents, calmed down a riot as some Bajorans attempted to flee the station by encouraging them to defend their home, and helped defend the station against [[General]] {{dis|Krim|General}}'s troops, who attempted to take the station by force. After capturing Krim, Li was able to explain that the ''coup'' was being orchestrated by the Cardassians. Krim told his troops to stand down. Li was killed while saving Sisko from an attack by [[Colonel]] {{dis|Day|Colonel}}, and as a result, became a hero both in legend and reality. ({{DS9|The Siege}}) ==Legacy== [[File:Li Nalas on tarot card.jpg|thumb|Li Nalas on the "Invasion" tarot card]] [[Shaxs]] owned a set of Bajoran [[tarot card]]s, of which the "Invasion" card depicted Li Nalas in the Hutet labor camp, facing off against a Cardassian soldier with a [[sword]]. ({{LD|Empathological Fallacies}}) == Memorable quotes == "''Well, I consider myself something of a history buff and I must say some of the campaigns you led against the Cardassians were truly remarkable examples of tactical-''"
"''Doctor, I think you'll find that others enjoy talking about those days more than I do.''"
"''Of course. I understand ''completely''.''"
:- Doctor '''Julian Bashir''' and '''Li Nalas''' ({{DS9|The Homecoming}}) "''I thought they'd have forgotten me by now.''"
"''It appears you were wrong.''"
"''This morning I was a slave and tonight I'm a hero.''"
:- Commander '''Benjamin Sisko''' and '''Li Nalas''', on his popularity ({{DS9|The Homecoming}}) "''Where are you running to? This is Bajor. We're Bajorans. We fought a war to regain our homeland. How can you abandon it like frightened Cardassian voles? These ships are for our guests who must leave because it's no longer safe for them. We're Bajorans. I say we stay and solve our problems together. Are you willing to join me?''"
:- '''Li Nalas''', during the evacuation of non-Bajorans from Deep Space 9 ({{DS9|The Siege}}) "''Off the hook... after all...''"
:- The last words of '''Li Nalas''', to Commander Sisko ({{DS9|The Siege}}) == Appendices == === Appearances === * {{DS9}} ** {{e|The Homecoming}} ** {{e|The Circle}} ** {{e|The Siege}} === Background information === Li Nalas was played by [[Richard Beymer]] in his only ''[[Star Trek]]'' appearance. His jacket from "The Homecoming" was sold off on the [[It's A Wrap! sale and auction]] on eBay. {{stala|9302}} The {{Star Trek Minutiae|resources/scripts/422.txt|script}} for "The Homecoming" states the pronunciation of Li's name is "LEE NAH-less." Furthermore, it describes him as "''a tall, rangy, laconic Bajoran in his late forties ''[…]'' a man of great physical presence, has a quiet self-effacing [[Abraham Lincoln]]/[[Gary Cooper]] charisma. He's intensely self-conscious; but years of living with his reputation has taught him to hide his true feelings behind his public image.''" (''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine Companion - A Series Guide and Script Library]]'') The writers briefly considered having Li survive the final episode of the trilogy and become a recurring character. Both [[Peter Allan Fields]] and [[Michael Piller]] supported this idea; "''It seemed to me that killing him would send us back to square one,''" said Fields, "''Why go through three episodes with this guy, and then let him die? You're back as if he'd never been around. We could have written the whole thing without him.''" The final decision, however, came down to [[Ira Steven Behr]], who believed that the character's death was truly necessary for the episode; "''I just felt that this was a man who was living a lie, and at the end there needed to be a form of redemption, one that involved some self-sacrifice. The character was so impotent in certain ways, so out of his depth, and so clearly miserable as this figurehead. I think death really was, at that point, a blessing for him…''" As executive producer, Behr also had the practical concerns to think about. From a production standpoint, he didn't know how easy it would be to get Richard Beymer back to reprise the role, or how much it would cost to hire him. Ultimately, the writers decided they did need someone to fulfill Li's role and so the character of [[Shakaar Edon]] was created in the [[DS9 Season 3|third season]]. ({{ds9c|83}}) In their review of "The Siege", authors [[Mark Jones]] and [[Lance Parkin]] wrote of Li Nalas, "''It's odd that they kill Li Nalas after so much build up. But this is another strong episode.''" (''[[Beyond the Final Frontier]]'', p. 193) === Apocrypha === Li Nalas appears in the ''[[Star Trek: Terok Nor]]'' novel ''[[Dawn of the Eagles]]'', which features his capture by the Cardassians. In the ''{{dis|Star Trek: Section 31|novel series}}'' novel ''[[Abyss]]'', and the [[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine - Mission Gamma|''Mission Gamma'']] novels ''[[Cathedral]]'' and ''[[Lesser Evil]]'', the Bajoran Militia name their ship-of-state the ''Li Nalas'' in his honor. In the [[Pocket DS9]] novel ''[[Rising Son]]'', [[Jake Sisko]] discusses the return of Li Nalas with [[Opaka|Opaka Sulan]]. His [[mirror universe]] {{mb|Li Nalas (mirror)|counterpart}} is depicted as being the [[Prime minister|First Minister]] of [[Bajor#Parallel universes|Bajor]] in ''[[Obsidian Alliances#Saturn's Children|Saturn's Children]]''. === External link === * {{mbeta}} [[de:Li Nalas]] [[es:Li Nalas]] [[fr:Li Nalas]] [[nl:Li Nalas]] [[Category:Bajorans]] [[Category:Bajoran Militia personnel]] [[Category:Deep Space 9 personnel]] [[Category:Bajoran government officials]] [[Category:Terok Nor residents]]

{{sidebar individual |image = Furel.jpg |caption = Furel |species = [[Bajoran]] |affiliation = [[Shakaar resistance cell]] (formerly) |occupation = [[Resistance fighter]] (formerly) |status = [[Deceased]], killed by [[Silaran Prin]] |datestatus = 2373 |died = [[2373]],
[[Deep Space 9]] |actor = [[William Lucking]] }} '''Furel''' was a member of the [[Shakaar resistance cell]] and an intimate friend of [[Lupaza]]. In [[2355]], Furel met young [[Kira Nerys]], who wanted to join [[Bajoran Resistance|the resistance]]. Although he and the rest of the {{dis|cell|organization}} found Kira too young, Lupaza stood up for her. When he made [[joke]]s about Kira, he was often hit by Lupaza for doing so. Several years later, when [[Kira Taban]], Nerys' father, was driven from his homestead and mortally wounded by the Cardassians, Furel accompanied her to take revenge against the [[Ninth Order]]. Afterwards, and standing by her father's grave, Furel asked Nerys whether he should get the others for a ceremony, but she declined, and told him she wanted to attack the Cardassians again right away. ({{DS9|Ties of Blood and Water}}) At some point of time after that, before a mission to rescue a number of his comrades, Furel prayed to the [[Prophet]]s, offering his own life in exchange for success in saving his endangered friends. The mission was a success, but Furel lost his left arm. Furel felt the Prophets had been generous and, years later, he declined a [[Furel's doctor 001|Federation doctor]]'s offer of a replacement, believing it would have been an ungrateful act to the Prophets. After the [[Occupation of Bajor]] ended, he went on to become a [[farmer]]. In [[2371]], [[Shakaar Edon|Shakaar]] refused to return [[soil reclamator]]s to [[Kai]] [[Winn Adami|Winn]], who had become acting [[prime minister|first minister]] of [[Bajor]]. When Winn sent the [[Bajoran Militia]] to arrest Shakaar, Furel – together with Lupaza, Kira, and most of the other former members of the Shakaar resistance cell – joined Shakaar in resisting the kai. ({{DS9|Shakaar}}) In [[2373]], Furel visited Kira on [[starbase]] [[Deep Space 9]] with Lupaza, because someone was [[death|killing]] their former resistance comrades. After [[stowaway|stowing away]] aboard a [[Bajoran transport ship 001|transport ship]] they sneaked aboard DS9 unnoticed by [[beam]]ing directly into [[Chief]] [[Miles O'Brien|O'Brien]]'s [[quarters|bedroom]], their assailant, [[Silaran Prin]], knew where they were and planted an [[bomb|explosive device]] on the [[space station|station]]'s window, by means of a [[hunter probe]]. When it exploded, the room decompressed and Furel was killed, as was Lupaza. The Prophets spoke, I answered their call!|Neela|2369|In the Hands of the Prophets}} '''Neela''' was a [[female]] [[Bajoran]] and a member of the [[Bajoran Militia]] during the late [[24th century]]. In [[2369]], Neela served on the [[space station]] [[Deep Space 9]] as an [[engineer]] under [[Operations Chief]] [[Miles O'Brien]]. As part of her duties, she once helped to repair [[Lieutenant]] [[Jadzia Dax]]'s [[science]] station following a malfunction. ({{DS9|Duet}}) Neela became involved in a plot to kill [[Vedek]] [[Bareil Antos]], ostensibly to ensure the succession of Vedek [[Winn Adami|Winn]] after the departure of [[Kai]] [[Opaka]]. First, she planned an escape route to a [[runabout]] from the [[Promenade]], and killed [[Ensign]] [[Aquino]] after he caught her doing so. She left him in an area to make it appear he had accidentally killed himself while fixing a [[power conduit]]. Second, she planted a bomb in the station's school during Winn's argument with [[Keiko O'Brien]] about her secular approach to teaching. This had the planned effect of convincing Bareil to come to the station, where she would kill him in public and flee. When O'Brien and [[Odo]] found out about the escape route and secured the area, Neela went to Winn to express her second thoughts about the [[assassination]]. Winn told her [[Prophet]]s sometimes ask for large sacrifices, and encouraged her to continue with the plan, knowing she would be caught. She agreed, and set out to complete the plan, however, [[Commander]] [[Benjamin Sisko]] and [[Senior chief petty officer|Chief]] O'Brien managed to discover Neela's intentions and stopped her before she could kill Bareil. Neela was subsequently taken into custody, but refused to implicate Winn, insisting that she had answered the call of the Prophets. ({{DS9|In the Hands of the Prophets}}) == Appendices == === Background information === Neela was played by actress [[Robin Christopher]]. The script for "Duet" describes Neela as a Bajoran "engineering apprentice". It further gives the pronunciation of her name as "''NEE-la''". {{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/419.txt}} In contrast, the script for "In the Hands of the Prophets" gives the pronunciation as "''NEE-luh''". She is also described as being, "''in her early twenties, bright, pretty, and eager to please.''" {{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/420.txt}} Neela was originally supposed to appear in three episodes of the season, making her debut in {{e|The Forsaken}} with the aim of making the audience believe she was to be a new recurring character so as not to make it obvious she was the villain. Unfortunately, the producers decided that the actress playing [[Anara]] in that episode wasn't the right type to be an assassin and so the role was recast as Neela. In the story treatment, Neela was to be killed to silence her. A leftover reference to Anara can still be seen in the final episode in the form of the computer code O'Brien and Dax break, which spells out "A-N-A-R-A". ({{ds9c|66}}; ''[[The Making of Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'', p. 302) === External links === * {{mbeta}} [[de:Neela]] [[es:Neela]] [[fr:Neela]] [[Category:Bajorans]] [[Category:Bajoran Militia personnel]] [[Category:Deep Space 9 personnel]]

[[Military]] [[Officer]] |sibling = [[Bajoran Gallitep brother 001|Lenaris' brother]] |status = Active |datestatus = 2371 |actor = [[John Doman]] }} [[Colonel]] '''Lenaris Holem''' was a [[male]] [[Bajoran]] [[military]] [[officer]] in the [[Bajoran Militia]] in the late-[[24th century]]. During the [[Cardassian]] [[Occupation of Bajor]], he was a member of the [[Ornathia resistance cell]] where he once led a raid on [[Pullock V]], a Cardassian [[planet]]. It was the first off-world raid against the [[Cardassian Union]]. During the Occupation, [[Bajoran Gallitep brother 001|his brother]] was freed from the [[Gallitep]] labor camp by [[Kira Nerys]] and the [[Shakaar resistance cell]]. After the Occupation ended in [[2369]], he joined the [[Bajoran Militia]] and by [[2371]], he had risen to the rank of colonel. Later that year, he led the several troops in [[Dahkur Province]] on a mission to find [[Shakaar Edon]] and the rest of his resistance cell, which had defied [[Winn Adami]] by not returning several government-owned [[soil reclamator]]s. Winn had ordered the Militia to take over the search from the [[Bajoran civil police|civil police]]. Lenaris later agreed with Shakaar that Bajorans fighting each other could lead to a violent [[civil war]] and so stood down his forces. He later consulted with his fellow officers, who agreed to support Shakaar in the election for [[First Minister]]. ({{DS9|Shakaar}}) == Appendices == === Background information === The script for "Shakaar" describes Lenaris as a veteran military officer, having "''been in too many combat situations to be taken aback by anything''" when he is surrounded by Kira and Shakaar's men. {{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/470.txt}} === Apocrypha === Lenaris appears in the [[Deep Space Nine relaunch|DS9 relaunch]] novel ''{{dis|Unity|novel}}'', where he is one of the top officers in the Bajoran Militia holding the rank of [[general]]. He was also one of the signatories to Bajor's admittance into the Federation. He also appears in the second novel of the [[Star Trek: Terok Nor|''Terok Nor'' trilogy]], ''[[Night of the Wolves]]''. He is one of the protagonists in the novel, which depicts his life during the Occupation. Lenaris is depicted as a pilot, which leads to his participation in the Pullock V raid in [[2348]]. In ''[[Obsidian Alliances#Saturn's Children|Saturn's Children]]'', his [[mirror universe]] {{mb|Lenaris Holem (mirror)|counterpart}} was mentioned as being a prominent member of the [[Council of Ministers]] and a close friend of {{mu|Leeta}}'s father. === External links === * {{mbeta}} [[de:Lenaris Holem]] [[es:Lenaris Holem]] [[fr:Lenaris Holem]] [[nl:Lenaris Holem]] [[pl:Lenaris Holem]] [[Category:Bajorans]] [[Category:Bajoran Militia personnel]]

'''Baltrim''' was a male [[Bajoran]] [[farmer]] who, along with [[Keena]], had been rendered {{dis|mute|disorder}} by the [[Cardassian]]s during the [[Occupation of Bajor]]. In [[2351]], Baltrim and Keena managed to escape to the Bajoran [[moon]] [[Jeraddo]], where they resided in a [[cottage]], close to their friend, a fellow farmer named [[Mullibok]].

However, in [[2369]], plans were underway to transfer [[energy]] from Jeraddo's core, forcing the evacuation of all of Jeraddo's residents. Mullibok, however, refused to allow himself or his friends to be taken from their home.

After initial attempts to convince them to leave were unsuccessful, [[Major]] [[Kira Nerys]] [[transporter|transported]] to the moon's surface with two [[security]] guards to remove them by force. After a brief struggle, both Baltrim and Keena were evacuated. Mullibok, who was injured, remained behind. He was evacuated soon afterwards after Kira destroyed his cottage, giving them no further reason to remain. ({{DS9|Progress}})

{{bginfo|Baltrim was played by actor [[Terrence Evans]].|According to the script for ''Progress'', Baltrim was in his 40s in 2369.}}

'''Nevala''' was a [[female]] [[Romulan]] [[officer]] in the [[24th century]] [[Romulan Star Empire]]. 

In [[2374]], she was [[CO|second in command]] of a squad of Romulans led by [[Rekar]] who captured the {{USS|Prometheus|Prometheus class}}, a [[prototype]] long-range [[Starfleet]] [[starship]]. On orders from Rekar, the team killed the whole crew, though Nevala preferred having someone able to help learn the ship's systems. 

Unbeknownst to Nevala, [[The Doctor]] had been transferred from the {{USS|Voyager}} and made plans to stop the group along with the ''Prometheus''{{'}} [[EMH Mark II]]. Nevala brought an injured Romulan of the team to the ship's sickbay and encountered The Doctor, believing his explanation that he was the ship's [[EMH]] after a bit of questioning. Rekar and Nevala accepted that The Doctor was doing medical scans on the [[bridge]] until he accessed a console. Rekar detained him while Nevala found out that a [[hologram]] had been transferred on the ship. She joined Rekar to [[interrogate]] him and, when it was apparent he would not admit any information other than a story she didn't believe, she suggested a complete [[algorithm]] extraction. She started working on it when she and the other Romulans were rendered unconscious by [[neurozine]] [[gas]], introduced into the [[ventilation system]] by the EMH Mark II. She was unconscious and captured when the vessel was then returned to Starfleet control. ({{VOY|Message in a Bottle}})
